title: Grakern: A Lawful Graph-Kernel Calculus and Compiler
productThesis: Grakern is a small calculus of lawful kernels and graph decompositions together with a compiler that lowers semantic expressions to exact sparse features, hierarchy intersection, Gale operators, or pairwise plans. Standard graph kernels are recipes over shared semantic computations rather than isolated estimator classes.
successCriterion: One exact semantic computation supports multiple lawful kernels, multiple numerical views, correct out-of-sample behavior, and one optimized execution plan without duplicating algorithm-specific machinery.

firstArchitecturalProof.name: Paired Weisfeiler-Lehman subtree and optimal-assignment slice
firstArchitecturalProof.requiredOutcome: One immutable exact WL refinement trace feeds exact subtree features and exact threshold-expanded optimal-assignment features, which combine by direct sum and produce a Gale Gram matrix, a Gale-backed operator, correct train-query cross values, complete query norms, and intelligible provenance.
firstArchitecturalProof.failurePolicy: If this slice requires duplicated traces, mutable query state, opaque pattern identity, or algorithm-specific preparation paths, reopen the architecture ADRs before adding more kernels.

principles: Mathematical semantics and finite computational realizations are separate contracts.
Graph identity is distinct from node and edge data.
Session sharing, semantic reproducibility, and prepared-artifact identity are distinct.
Exact feature availability is a planned capability, not a type-level property of every kernel.
Mathematical closure laws do not authorize floating-point reassociation.
Gale owns matrices, sparse matrices, vectors, operators, and numerical backends.
Grakern owns kernel semantics, sample alignment, feature identity, query alignment, provenance, audits, and plan explanations.
Ravel is not an initial dependency.
Every specialized semantic node has an independent denotation and reference interpreter.
The v0.1 compiler is closed and exhaustively matched.

gale.prohibition: Do not build reproducible Grakern artifacts against unrelated dirty sibling-worktree changes.

ravel.reason: Dense and sparse mathematical matrix ownership belongs to Gale; Grakern has no initial n-dimensional array requirement.

pairwiseTypes.name: PairScore[A]
pairwiseTypes.claim: Arbitrary real-valued pair score; may be asymmetric.

pairwiseTypes.name: Kernel[A]
pairwiseTypes.claim: Symmetric positive-semidefinite kernel by safe construction.

pairwiseTypes.name: StrongKernel[A]
pairwiseTypes.claim: Nonnegative kernel satisfying the strong-kernel inequality.

strongKernelRules: StrongKernel is a semantic claim and is not identified with a finite hierarchy.
A finite hierarchy is a certified realization that enables histogram-intersection lowering.
Delta is strong on any lawful equality domain without globally enumerating that domain.
Strong pullback and nonnegative constant scaling preserve StrongKernel.
Sum and product of strong kernels return Kernel.
Normalization and induced Gaussianization return Kernel.
Optimal assignment accepts StrongKernel and uses hierarchy intersection when realizable or padded Hungarian assignment otherwise.

decomposition.execution: Fused fold or emitter; materialization exists only for reference testing.
decomposition.deferred: Signed coefficients will use a separate FiniteLinearCombination abstraction.

graphContract.identityRule: V is graph-local identity; N and E are attributes. Equal N values never merge vertices.
graphContract.factoryRule: The preferred factory receives one graph4s.Graph[V] and derives total node and edge fields from total functions.
graphContract.sampleScoping: Different samples may reuse the same V values. Corpus packing assigns disjoint internal offsets.
graphContract.packedOwnership: PackedGraphCorpus is private Grakern execution state and not a second public graph model.
graphContract.genericGraphSource: Deferred until the graph4s walking slice proves the boundary.

hierarchyAndAssignment.rootPolicy: Root height is finite and nonnegative but need not be zero.
hierarchyAndAssignment.paddingPolicy: Unequal bags are padded semantically with an external zero-feature dummy that is not required to be a hierarchy leaf.
hierarchyAndAssignment.histogramFormula: Sum over hierarchy nodes of incrementalHeight(node) * min(countLeft(node), countRight(node)).
hierarchyAndAssignment.thresholdFeature: HierarchyFeature(node, multiplicityThreshold) has value sqrt(incrementalHeight(node)) when the bag count below node reaches that threshold.
hierarchyAndAssignment.thresholdComplexity: The number of active threshold features for a bag is O(number of items times hierarchy depth).

levels.name: SemanticFingerprint
levels.availability: only when every semantic component has a stable descriptor
levels.purpose: identify the represented denotation to the degree asserted by descriptors

levels.name: ArtifactFingerprint
levels.availability: only when semantic and corpus identity are durable

projectionPolicy: Projection.named carries a user-asserted stable id and version.
A name and version do not prove that the closure implementation is unchanged.
Anonymous closures remain executable and disable durable caching when necessary.
identityAndFingerprinting.reporting: Plan reports enumerate every fingerprint blocker.

refinementContract.semanticIdentity: Exact recursive signatures and their parent relation are semantics; integer colours are trace-local encodings.
refinementContract.nextSignature: previous own signature plus the exact multiset of edge-key and neighbor-signature pairs
requirements: hashes accelerate lookup but never define equality
collisions resolve through exact structural comparison
colour ids never escape without their owning trace
parent links connect adjacent exact signatures
training trace and interner are immutable
query refinement uses an immutable overlay or fork
concurrent query batches cannot change prepared state
query-only descendants may share known ancestors
anonymous labels may disable durable fingerprints
refinementContract.representationConstraint: Use hash-consed or interned DAG nodes; do not repeatedly materialize recursive signature trees.

numericalContract.nonFinitePolicy: Reject NaN and both infinities at validated boundaries.
numericalContract.negativeZeroPolicy: Canonicalize negative zero to positive zero in nonnegative wrappers unless an ADR-approved operation requires raw signed zero.
numericalContract.projectionValidation: Validate projected numeric values once during packing or preparation and then use trusted primitive columns.

normalization.negativeDiagonal: A diagonal below minus epsilon is an error.
normalization.nearZeroDiagonal: A diagonal with absolute value at most epsilon is treated as zero and records an audit event.
normalization.zeroNorm: All normalized values involving a zero-norm object are zero, including its self-kernel.

floatingExecution: Do not distribute products over sums.
Do not reassociate sums merely because mathematical closure permits it.
Use deterministic partitioning and fixed reduction trees.
Use exact equality for combinatorial identities and declared tolerances for general numeric primitives.
Do not publish a Cats CommutativeSemiring instance in v0.1.

preparedOutputs.featureCapability: prepared.features returns a typed unavailable result when no selected exact realization exists.
preparedOutputs.operatorCapability: An operator is semantically available for every finite reference corpus and may be feature-backed, Gram-backed, or pairwise-tiled.

queryFeatures.rule: Query-only coordinates contribute to complete query norms but not nonexistent train-query cross terms.

compilerContract.v0_1Shape: Closed internal GADT or sealed hierarchy with exhaustive compiler matching.
prohibitions: no generic rewrite framework before two vertical slices
compilerContract.specializedNodeRule: A specialized semantic primitive is acceptable when it has an independent denotation and reference interpreter.

pipeline: train-query aligned features and cross matrix
walkingSlice.planInvariant: One WL refinement plan node has two consumers.
queryCases: multiplicity threshold larger than any training graph

acceptanceCourt.name: vertex-reindexing invariance
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Arbitrary graph vertex permutations preserve kernel values.

acceptanceCourt.name: exact collision handling
acceptanceCourt.requirement: A deliberately constant or adversarial hash does not change results.

acceptanceCourt.name: shared execution
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Subtree plus OA executes one refinement per graph and round.

acceptanceCourt.name: OA oracle
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Hierarchy intersection agrees with padded Hungarian assignment on repeated and unequal bags.

acceptanceCourt.name: reference differential
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Independent scalar denotation and optimized feature realizations agree.

acceptanceCourt.name: train-cross coherence
acceptanceCourt.requirement: cross(train) agrees with gram under the declared numerical policy.

acceptanceCourt.name: query-only feature norm
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Unseen query features alter query self-kernels but not unmatched cross terms.

acceptanceCourt.name: ancestor sharing
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Unseen query leaves receive partial OA similarity through shared known ancestors.

acceptanceCourt.name: feature reconstruction
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Subtree and threshold OA feature dot products reconstruct component kernels.

acceptanceCourt.name: deterministic execution
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Fixed partitioning and reduction trees yield reproducible results.

acceptanceCourt.name: provenance
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Every nonzero contribution traces to round, signature, hierarchy node, and threshold.

acceptanceCourt.name: plan sharing
acceptanceCourt.requirement: The plan contains one WL node and two consumers.

acceptanceCourt.name: prepared immutability
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Repeated and concurrent query overlays do not mutate prepared training state.

acceptanceCourt.name: operator agreement
acceptanceCourt.requirement: Feature-backed operator application agrees with materialized Gram multiplication.

compatibilityCourt.purpose: Detect compatibility drift against deliberately aligned GraKeL behavior without treating GraKeL as the semantic oracle.
execution: A pinned Python environment regenerates versioned JSON fixtures from GraKeL.
Ordinary Scala tests consume committed fixtures and do not require Python or GraKeL.
A scheduled or explicit refresh job reruns the external oracle and fails on fixture drift.
Each fixture records graph encoding, kernel parameters, train-query split, normalization, and expected matrix ordering.
firstTargets: WL subtree with aligned round convention and categorical node labels
WL optimal assignment with aligned hierarchy depth and categorical node labels
exclusions: query-only behavior where GraKeL does not expose the same semantic contract
edge-aware WL variants until both libraries use the same signature definition
any mismatch caused by documented iteration, normalization, unknown-label, or input-conversion conventions
compatibilityCourt.claimPolicy: A parity pass means Grakern reproduces the declared GraKeL configuration on the recorded fixtures. It does not establish kernel validity, prove equivalence outside those fixtures, or override Grakern's independent denotation.

alphaScope: soft shortest path when the exact pairwise path is ready
GraKeL parity fixtures for deliberately aligned kernels

requiredRows: query cross at several novel-feature rates
sparse and increasingly dense feature matrices
performanceCourt.claimPolicy: No performance claim is made from microbenchmarks alone or before end-to-end semantic parity.

stopConditions: Subtree and OA require separate refinement traces.
Query evaluation mutates prepared training state.
Vertex permutation changes exact kernel values.
Hash collisions change feature or hierarchy identity.
A colour id escapes without its owning trace.
Corpus artifacts are keyed only by sample names.
WL OA is exposed as linear features without a valid feature map.
Query-only features are omitted from normalized query norms.
Ravel becomes necessary merely to represent matrices.
Compiler optimization requires unreported floating reassociation.
A GraKeL compatibility fixture is used as the semantic definition of a kernel.
A within-graph commute-time node kernel is mislabeled as a kernel between graph samples.
Packing requires access to graph4s private arrays.
A specialized lowering lacks an independent denotation.
The feature-backed operator disagrees with the Gram realization beyond tolerance.

policy: Gate issues carry the actual blocking dependencies.
A later epic and each of its root tasks are blocked by the previous gate.
Closing an epic is distinct from closing its children or passing its gate.
PRD, Git, Mote, and publication state are reported independently.

beads.title: E0 Architecture freeze and project foundation
beads.body: Bootstrap the project and freeze six executable ADRs before kernel implementation. Exit through Gate A only after compiling positive and negative contract probes.

beads.title: Bootstrap reproducible multi-module build and CI
beads.body: Initialize Git and the Typelevel-style Scala 3.7.4 build, add JVM/JS/Native semantic modules and JVM engine scaffolding, pin clean graph4s and Gale source revisions, and add baseline format/compile/test checks.

beads.title: ADR-001 Graph identity and GraphSample
beads.body: Freeze graph-local identity, total node and edge fields, topology-first construction, sample scoping, and private corpus packing.

beads.title: ADR-002 Strong kernels, hierarchy, bags, and optimal assignment
beads.body: Separate StrongKernel semantics from finite hierarchy realization; specify positive-root hierarchies, external-zero padding, multiplicities, Hungarian fallback, and histogram-intersection capability.

beads.title: ADR-003 Plan, semantic, and artifact identity
beads.body: Freeze PlanNodeId, SemanticFingerprint, ArtifactFingerprint, projection durability, corpus content identity, and explicit fingerprint blockers.

beads.title: ADR-004 Numerical domain, normalization, and decomposition weights
beads.body: Freeze finite scalar validation, negative-zero handling, checked preparation, zero-norm normalization, deterministic floating schedules, and nonnegative v0.1 decomposition weights.

beads.title: ADR-005 Prepared capabilities and Gale ownership
beads.body: Freeze optional exact features, universal operator semantics, FeatureMatrix, AlignedFeatures, novelSquaredNorm, Gale payload ownership, Grakern metadata ownership, and Alder boundary.

beads.title: ADR-006 Refinement and pattern identity
beads.body: Freeze exact recursive signatures, collision resolution, trace-local IDs, immutable query overlays, ancestor sharing, durable codecs, and DAG representation.

beads.title: Compile architecture contract probes
beads.body: Compile positive examples and compile-fail invalid examples for all six ADRs. Demonstrate module acyclicity and that anonymous closures cannot acquire durable fingerprints.

beads.title: Gate A: architecture contracts frozen
beads.body: Pass only when the build exists, all ADRs are versioned and consistent, contract probes behave as designed, core imports neither graph4s nor Gale, and no unresolved ownership contradiction remains.

beads.title: E1 Minimal semantic and graph walking skeleton
beads.body: Implement only enough semantic core, hierarchy reference behavior, GraphSample, and packed corpus state to support one end-to-end WL walking skeleton.

beads.title: Implement validated scalars and typed preparation errors
beads.body: Add finite scalar wrappers, checked constructors, negative-zero policy, projection diagnostics, and typed expected failure channels.

beads.title: Implement PairScore, Similarity, Kernel, and StrongKernel skeleton
beads.body: Add safe and unsafe constructors, minimal closed expression nodes, named algebraic operations, strong return-type rules, and independent scalar evaluation.

beads.title: Implement projections and three-level fingerprint metadata
beads.body: Implement ephemeral and named projections, PlanNodeId, fingerprintability blockers, semantic fingerprint composition, and artifact-fingerprint input records.

beads.title: Implement FiniteBag, hierarchy validation, and Hungarian OA reference
beads.body: Implement exact bag multiplicity, positive-root hierarchy validation, LCA evaluation, external-zero padding, strong realization metadata, and a padded Hungarian reference evaluator.

beads.title: Implement graph4s-backed GraphSample
beads.body: Add topology-first total field construction, graph-local vertex identity, sample keys, graph-scoped field validation, and molecular examples using AtomId rather than Atom identity.

beads.title: Implement private packed graph corpus
beads.body: Pack graph offsets, CSR adjacency, ownership, projected categorical columns, projected numeric columns, source diagnostics, and provenance mapping through graph4s public APIs.

beads.title: Connect minimal semantic core to one packed graph
beads.body: Demonstrate fallible preparation from GraphSample through PackedGraphCorpus into a minimal semantic node without building a general compiler framework.

beads.title: Gate B: minimal walking skeleton is executable
beads.body: Pass when GraphSample, packing, minimal kernel semantics, hierarchy reference behavior, and fingerprint metadata form one executable, typed, reproducible skeleton.

beads.title: E2 Exact immutable Weisfeiler-Lehman trace
beads.body: Implement exact recursive WL identity, collision-safe interning, trace-local colours, parent links, immutable query overlays, and invariance laws.

beads.title: Define exact WL signature and provenance model
beads.body: Represent initial and recursive edge-aware multiset signatures, semantic parent links, levels, stable descriptors when available, and source provenance.

beads.title: Implement collision-safe WL signature interner
beads.body: Use hashes only for candidate buckets, resolve equality structurally, intern DAG nodes, and keep integer IDs trace-local.

beads.title: Build exact batch WL refinement traces
beads.body: Compute per-level vertex colours and signature parent links from packed corpora while preserving order-independent semantics and exact pattern identity.

beads.title: Implement immutable query refinement overlay
beads.body: Fork or overlay the training interner immutably, reuse known signatures and ancestors, assign query-local new IDs, and support concurrent deterministic queries.

beads.title: Prove WL identity, collision, reindexing, and query laws
beads.body: Add adversarial-hash, vertex-permutation, trace ownership, parent-chain, query-overlay immutability, and concurrent-query regression suites.

beads.title: Gate C: exact WL trace semantics certified
beads.body: Pass when exact signatures survive adversarial collisions and vertex permutations, query overlays are immutable, parent links are correct, and colour IDs remain trace-scoped.

beads.title: E3 Paired WL subtree and optimal-assignment features
beads.body: Make one exact WL trace support subtree features, hierarchy OA, threshold-expanded exact OA features, direct-sum composition, normalization, and provenance.

beads.title: Implement exact WL subtree sparse features
beads.body: Emit counts keyed by round and exact signature with per-round nonnegative feature scaling and complete provenance.

beads.title: Derive WL hierarchy realization from refinement parent links
beads.body: Construct the finite observed WL hierarchy, nonnegative level increments, synthetic zero root where appropriate, leaf multiplicities, and strong-kernel realization metadata.

beads.title: Implement padded Hungarian WL-OA oracle
beads.body: Evaluate WL vertex bags through the strong base evaluator with repeated elements and unequal cardinalities for independent reference comparison.

beads.title: Implement hierarchy-intersection WL-OA evaluator
beads.body: Compute incremental-height histogram intersection and prove agreement with the padded Hungarian oracle.

beads.title: Implement exact WL-OA threshold features
beads.body: Emit hierarchy-node and multiplicity-threshold features scaled by square-root incremental height; verify O(vertices times depth) active-coordinate growth and exact kernel reconstruction.

beads.title: Compose subtree and OA by direct sum and normalize
beads.body: Concatenate exact feature blocks, apply square-root kernel weights, compute complete diagonals, apply the normalization policy, and retain component provenance.

beads.title: Implement WL contribution provenance
beads.body: Trace subtree and OA feature contributions to component, round, exact signature, hierarchy node, multiplicity threshold, and representative source vertices.

beads.title: Gate D: paired exact WL feature proof
beads.body: Pass when one trace feeds both exact feature families, OA intersection and threshold features agree with Hungarian reference, direct-sum features reconstruct the combined normalized kernel, and provenance is complete.

beads.title: Bootstrap pinned GraKeL WL parity fixtures
beads.body: Generate committed GraKeL 0.1.10 fixtures for the aligned WL subtree and WL optimal-assignment pair/path corpus, add ordinary Scala regression tests that consume the JSON without Python, and provide an explicit pinned regeneration check.

beads.title: E4 Closed compiler, Gale outputs, and query alignment
beads.body: Compile the paired WL expression to exact Gale features, Gram and operator views, immutable aligned query features, complete query norms, and a transparent plan report.

beads.title: Implement closed exhaustive v0.1 compiler
beads.body: Pattern-match the small sealed IR, discover shared plan nodes, analyze capabilities, schedule WL trace sharing, and select exact feature-backed realizations without a public lowering SPI.

beads.title: Implement plan sharing and semantic/artifact fingerprint reporting
beads.body: Assign PlanNodeIds, compose semantic fingerprints when durable, derive artifact fingerprints from corpus and engine inputs, and enumerate blockers.

beads.title: Materialize exact Gale training feature matrices
beads.body: Build Gale CSR values with SampleIndex, FeatureDictionary, FeatureMetadata, stable block ordering, and no Ravel dependency.

beads.title: Implement Gale Gram and feature-backed operator views
beads.body: Produce metadata-bearing Gram matrices and DoubleLinearOperator realizations, then verify operator application against materialized Gram multiplication.

beads.title: Implement aligned query features and complete query norms
beads.body: Build shared query CSR coordinates plus novelSquaredNorm, preserve OA ancestor matches, compute exact cross values, and keep prepared training state immutable across query calls.

beads.title: Implement capabilities and explainable plan report
beads.body: Report the one-to-many WL plan graph, fingerprints, blockers, exactness, feature counts, density, query alignment, selected Gram/operator realization, normalization, memory, and estimated cost.

beads.title: Gate E: executable paired WL architecture
beads.body: Pass when one WL trace yields exact subtree and OA features, a Gale Gram matrix, a feature-backed operator, correct query cross values and norms, immutable query overlays, and an intelligible plan report.

beads.title: E5 Acceptance court and generic core hardening
beads.body: Turn the paired slice into reusable lawful contracts only after the architecture proof passes; add the differential court, deterministic execution, generic extraction, histograms, cross-platform gates, and docs.

beads.title: Build the independent semantic differential court
beads.body: Compare scalar semantics, LCA hierarchy, Hungarian OA, histogram intersection, threshold dots, direct-sum features, Gram, operator, cross, and normalization through independent paths.

beads.title: Build the pinned GraKeL compatibility court
beads.body: Generate versioned fixtures with GraKeL 0.1.10 for deliberately aligned kernels; record graph encodings, parameters, ordering, train-query splits, normalization, tolerances, and exclusions; consume committed fixtures from Scala tests without making GraKeL the semantic oracle.

beads.title: Implement the full WL acceptance suite
beads.body: Implement reindexing, adversarial collision, sharing, OA oracle, query-only norm, ancestor sharing, provenance, concurrency, plan-sharing, feature reconstruction, and operator-agreement tests.

beads.title: Implement deterministic parallel execution
beads.body: Use fixed partitioning and reduction trees, compare schedules, record numerical policy, and prove reproducibility without algebraic reassociation.

beads.title: Extract stable Decomposition, Refinement, Hierarchy, and feature contracts
beads.body: Generalize only contracts demonstrated by the WL slice, preserve reference interpreters, and keep compiler implementation details closed.

beads.title: Add vertex and edge histogram recipes
beads.body: Exercise generic decomposition and exact sparse feature paths with simple standard recipes and complete provenance.

beads.title: Complete cross-platform semantic gates and executable architecture docs
beads.body: Run supported JVM/JS/Native semantic and law suites, document the six ADRs and walking slice, compile examples, and distinguish JVM-engine-only functionality.

beads.title: Gate F: architecture validated and generic core hardened
beads.body: Pass when the full differential court succeeds, parallel execution is deterministic, extracted abstractions reduce duplication, histograms use the same machinery, and docs describe only implemented behavior.

beads.title: E6 Shortest-path second vertical slice
beads.body: Test decomposition, shared APSP, exact categorical features, nonnegative Dijkstra, continuous soft part kernels, endpoint canonicalization, and multiple lowerings for one denotation.

beads.title: Define shortest-path decomposition and endpoint semantics
beads.body: Define undirected endpoint canonicalization, path-part identity, disconnected pairs, distance semantics, and an independent materialized reference decomposition.

beads.title: Implement shared unweighted BFS APSP
beads.body: Compute exact integer all-pairs distances once per graph and share the transform across path-kernel consumers.

beads.title: Implement exact categorical shortest-path features
beads.body: Emit exact endpoint and integer-distance feature keys, reconstruct the reference kernel, and retain path provenance.

beads.title: Implement nonnegative finite weighted Dijkstra
beads.body: Validate edge lengths during packing, reject negative or nonfinite values, compute shared weighted APSP, and compare with the path denotation.

beads.title: Implement soft continuous shortest-path part kernel
beads.body: Combine categorical endpoint kernels with a continuous distance kernel through decomposition, exact pairwise evaluation, normalization, and typed numeric validation.

beads.title: Plan shared APSP and alternative shortest-path lowerings
beads.body: Share APSP nodes, choose BFS or Dijkstra from semantics, expose exact-feature versus pairwise capabilities, and explain the selection.

beads.title: Gate G: shortest-path slice validates the calculus
beads.body: Pass when decomposition is reusable, APSP is shared, exact categorical and soft pairwise paths agree with references, invalid weights fail early, and planner choice does not change denotation.

beads.title: E7 Alpha hardening and release evidence
beads.body: Complete prepared centering, user-facing documentation, end-to-end performance court, release acceptance audit, and a coherent alpha containing only proven kernels and views.

beads.title: Implement reference-bound prepared centering
beads.body: Center Gram, cross, features, and operator views against the training corpus without presenting centering as a context-free kernel.

beads.title: Build executable alpha documentation and examples
beads.body: Document GraphSample, lawful kernel construction, WL composition, shortest path, prepared views, query alignment, fingerprint blockers, provenance, and plan reports with compiled examples.

beads.title: Run end-to-end semantic and performance court
beads.body: Measure packing through Gram, cross, operator, and peak memory across WL feature/intersection strategies and query novelty levels; publish losses as well as wins.

beads.title: Produce alpha acceptance and release audit
beads.body: Audit module ownership, public API, laws, docs, dependency pins, binary/publication prerequisites, unsupported scope, and all stop conditions.

beads.title: Gate Alpha: coherent lawful graph-kernel calculus
beads.body: Pass when the alpha scope is implemented and verified, dependency and publication state are reported honestly, performance evidence is end-to-end, and no deferred catalogue promise leaks into the release claim.

beads.title: E8 Post-alpha computational breadth
beads.body: Add breadth only after the alpha proves the calculus: graphlets, explicit approximations, tiled output, implicit walks, directed support, adapters, and optional GPU work each retain a denotation and proof gate.

beads.title: Add exact and sampled graphlet recipes
beads.body: Implement canonical induced-subgraph patterns, exact enumeration, explicit sampling metadata, provenance, and reference agreement.

beads.title: Add RFF, Nyström, and feature-hashing realizations
beads.body: Push valid approximations through decompositions, record targets and seeds, preserve query norms, and expose approximation audit metadata.

beads.title: Add tiled and memory-mapped Gram output
beads.body: Add blocked matrix sinks, memory budgets, tiles, memory-mapped JVM output, and cancellation-safe ownership without making full dense Gram materialization mandatory.

beads.title: Add implicit product-graph random-walk kernels
beads.body: Define truncated and summable walk semantics, product-graph operators, solver strategies, convergence checks, residual diagnostics, and independent small-graph references.

beads.title: Add directed attributed graph support
beads.body: Extend graph4s field integration and packing only after a precise directed node/edge data contract and direction-sensitive kernel semantics are approved.

beads.title: Add Alder, I/O, and effect adapters
beads.body: Construct Alder-owned views, add dataset interchange modules, and provide optional Cats Effect and FS2 execution without infecting the mathematical API.

beads.title: Evaluate optional GPU lowerings
beads.body: Add GPU execution only for an existing semantic node with reference agreement, transfer-inclusive benchmarks, capability reporting, and no GPU type leakage into core.

beads.title: E9 Commute-time and resistance-distance kernels
beads.body: Add Laplacian-pseudoinverse commute-time kernels after first separating the lawful within-graph vertex kernel from any kernel between graph samples. Implement only graph-level lifts with an explicit denotation, independent reference, and invariance proof.

beads.title: Freeze commute-time domain and graph-level lift semantics
beads.body: Specify the weighted undirected graph contract, connected and disconnected behavior, Laplacian convention, volume scaling, the within-graph vertex kernel L+, its induced resistance or commute-time pseudometric, and any separate lawful lift that compares whole graph samples.

beads.title: Implement independent commute-time reference evaluator
beads.body: Compute small-graph Laplacians and Moore-Penrose pseudoinverses through an independent dense path; verify analytic paths, cycles, weighted graphs, component policy, PSD, centering, reindexing invariance, and effective-resistance identities.

beads.title: Implement exact and scalable commute-time lowerings
beads.body: Add the approved semantic node, Gale-backed dense spectral lowering, operator or linear-solve realization where justified, capability reporting, conditioning diagnostics, and deterministic numerical tolerances.

beads.title: Implement the approved graph-sample commute-time recipe
beads.body: Implement only the graph-level lift accepted by the semantics task, with a reference denotation, exact sample and feature identity, query behavior, provenance, and no comparison of unrelated raw L+ coordinates.

beads.title: Gate H: commute-time semantics and lowerings certified
beads.body: Pass when the within-graph kernel and graph-sample lift are not conflated, analytic and independent references agree, PSD and reindexing laws pass, disconnected and weighted behavior is explicit, and optimized lowerings report numerical limitations honestly.
